result.title: Beyond Prompt Imitation: Capability-Aware Video Generation with Smaller Models
result.summary: Inference-time methods that lift a small open video generator toward a proprietary one are compared through preference scores, which never say how much of the gap to a target video they close. We introduce the oracle control ladder, which hands a fixed student progressively richer information from a target clip and reads the closure of each fidelity metric at each rung as an empirical headroom reference for the methods that must synthesize that information. On 954 clips of the principal student, a dense caption reproduces little of the appearance and almost none of the motion of a target, a first frame closes half of the appearance gap and a tenth of the motion gap, a depth video closes three quarters of the motion gap and leaves color untouched, and the two together close 64 to 94% of every fidelity gap across four teachers, while a second student agrees on the rungs that it accepts. An item response model forecasts which rung closes which clip with held-out AUC of 0.76 to 0.95 on the fidelity criteria and serves as the prior of a budgeted selection policy. When controls are free, a fixed dense-control rung is hard to improve upon, and once controls are priced the policy lies above the fixed-rung frontier at matched cost and survives critics that ruin critic-driven search.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「oracle control ladder」，向小型视频生成器逐级提供目标片段的信息（dense caption、首帧、depth 视频等），用各保真度指标的闭合程度给出经验上限参照；并用 item response model 预测某一级信息能闭合哪个片段的哪项指标，作为预算受限选择策略的先验。
AI.relevance_reason: 按样本预测「追加某类信息/证据的收益」并在成本约束下选择信息层级，可能可供核查 LVR 中 LOOK 的证据筛选、动态获取与停止决策的收益-成本建模；但研究对象是视频生成保真度而非 latent 推理状态，联系需人工判断。
